Why specifications cannot predict exact game FPS.

Why cores, clocks, bandwidth, and synthetic scores do not equal a guaranteed frame rate.

01

Games stress systems differently

Engines vary in CPU scheduling, shaders, memory behavior, ray tracing, asset streaming, and driver optimization. The same GPU can produce very different results across games and settings.

02

The rest of the test system matters

Processor, RAM, cooling, power limits, driver, game patch, background tasks, resolution, upscaling, and scene selection all influence results.

03

Use reproducible tests

Prefer recent tests that disclose hardware, software, settings, run method, averages, and frame-time behavior. Specifications help explain a result; they are not a substitute for it.

Sources and verification

Use the exact product manuals and support lists linked from each catalog record. Industry specifications are maintained by organizations such as PCI-SIG, JEDEC, and NVM Express. Product implementations can be narrower than an industry standard.
